defects: All three kneeling boys (left boy in red fez, Mohammed in white, right boy in blue) hold their wooden slates flat and vertical directly in front of their faces like shields, completely hiding their faces instead of angling the slates to fan themselves.
Mohammed overlaps directly in front of the left boy in the red fez, creating a cluttered silhouette on screen left.
The right boy's left wrist and fingers twist and clip into the bottom edge of his slate.
The fqih sits passively with both hands on his knees instead of wiping his brow, and his crossed legs sink slightly into the wooden estrade surface.
tiles.fix: Lower and angle all three boys' slates to the side of their chests so their faces are visible while fanning, separate Mohammed rightward to clear the left boy, and raise the fqih's hand to wipe his brow.

defects: All three boys still hold their slates directly over their heads, leaving zero visible faces among the students.
Mohammed and the left boy in the red fez still overlap heavily on screen left.
The fqih in the background remains static with both hands resting on his knees instead of wiping his brow in the heat.
tiles.fix: Tilt and lower the boys' slates to reveal their faces at the opposite end of the fanning arc, unstack the two left boys horizontally, and animate the fqih wiping his forehead.

defects: In this medium crop, the two foreground boys (left boy in red fez and Mohammed) still have their faces completely hidden behind their slates and overlap each other directly in front of the camera.
The bottom of the frame slices awkwardly through the kneeling boys' shins and feet.
The fqih's raised right hand presses flat and stiffly against the side of his turban/temple rather than wiping across his brow.
tiles.fix: Lower the foreground boys' slates below chin level so their faces read clearly, reframe slightly higher or wider to clear the boys' overlapping bodies, and curve the fqih's hand across his forehead.

defects: The fqih's right foot and slipper clip into the raised stone threshold on the left side of the doorway.
The boy in the brown djellaba following behind in the exterior doorway is almost completely hidden behind the fqih's left arm and torso.
tiles.fix: Shift the fqih half a step forward and slightly screen left onto the interior tiled floor so his feet clear the threshold step and the boy entering behind him is visible in the doorway gap.

defects: Mohammed (right, white djellaba) has his back turned three-quarters to the camera facing back toward the doorway instead of walking into the sanctuary, hiding his face and slate.
Mohammed's left arm and hand clip into his torso and slate while pressed next to the boy in brown.
The fqih carries a student slate pressed to his chest with his left fingers clipping into the wood, and stares up at the empty upper-left wall instead of leading the boys.
Character scale is too small for the room: the adult fqih standing in front of the doorway is barely taller than the wooden tomb railing on the right.
tiles.fix: Scale the group up by roughly 20%, turn Mohammed to face into the room toward the camera with his slate held cleanly against his chest, and remove the student slate from the fqih while directing his gaze toward the room.

defects: On the far left, a woman in a red dress is inside/behind the wooden lattice of the tomb enclosure, appearing to walk through the solid catafalque instead of rounding the outside of the tomb.
On the far right edge, another woman in a red dress is sliced vertically in half by the frame border.
The central woman in the orange dress walks with hands clumped near her chest rather than clearly counting laps on her fingers.
tiles.fix: Move the path of the circling women outside the tomb railing and bring the far-right woman fully inside the frame while posing the central woman's hands clearly counting on her fingers.

defects: The two visible women (red dress on left, green dress on right) appear stalled facing each other near the middle of the floor rather than walking a continuous circular path around the tomb.
Neither woman shows a clear, readable finger-counting silhouette.
tiles.fix: Stage both women mid-stride along an elliptical loop around the tomb railing with the front woman's hands separated in profile so her raised counting fingers read against the wall.

defects: Mohammed is scaled far too small in the room—he stands shorter than the wooden tomb railing on the left and barely reaches the basin of the small wall fountain on the right.
His body is in a stiff, symmetrical default A-pose with arms flared slightly out from his sides, and his slate has vanished.
His eyes are open instead of closed for the deep breath beat.
tiles.fix: Scale Mohammed up by 25–30% to match the room architecture, close his eyes, expand his chest with shoulders relaxed out of the A-pose, and keep his slate tucked under one arm.

defects: In this closer crop of the deep-breath beat, Mohammed's eyes are wide open staring blankly upward to screen left instead of closed as directed.
His arms hang stiffly and symmetrically in an A-pose, and the bottom frame edge cuts right through his ankles.
tiles.fix: Close Mohammed's eyelids completely with a relaxed breathing expression, bend his elbows slightly out of the stiff A-pose, and crop slightly higher at mid-calf or wider to include his feet.

defects: The fqih does not raise a finger to his lips for silence: both arms remain down and his right sleeve hangs forward with the hand missing or clipped inside the cuff.
Framing is unbalanced, placing the fqih tightly against the left edge while leaving the right half of the frame empty.
tiles.fix: Pose the fqih's right hand raised in profile with his index finger touching his lips, and pan the crop slightly left to center him better.

defects: The two boys (brown djellaba and Mohammed in white) stand several feet out on the tiled floor away from the wall fountain on the far left, so their hands come nowhere near touching the fountain or water.
The fqih stands stiffly in the foreground facing away from the boys with both hands missing/clipped inside his hanging sleeves.
tiles.fix: Move both boys directly up to the left wall fountain basin with their hands extended into the water stream, and turn the fqih slightly toward them with visible hands clasped or resting naturally.

defects: The prayer group is not aligned in a row behind the master: the four boys cluster around the fqih's depth plane, and the second boy (brown djellaba) and Mohammed (white djellaba) overlap directly in front of the fqih from the camera view, hiding almost his entire body except the top of his turban.
The fqih is scaled far too small relative to the boys and room—he is barely taller than the young students standing directly behind him.
tiles.fix: Scale the fqih up to proper adult height, step him forward toward the front wall, and line the four boys up in a clean horizontal row behind him with spacing so the fqih is visible between the middle boys.

defects: During the ruku (bowing) beat, the fqih stands upright like a narrow white pillar while the boys bow behind him, violating the direction that the fqih leads ruku and the boys follow.
The boys only tilt slightly forward with stiff straight backs instead of bowing into a proper horizontal ruku with hands on knees, and the middle two boys still overlap the fqih's lower body.
tiles.fix: Pose the fqih and all four boys in a proper ruku bow (torsos bent forward near horizontal, hands resting on knees) with the boys spaced in a clean row behind the scaled-up fqih.

worst_problem: Key acting beats fail directly against director intent across the scene—boys hide their faces behind slates instead of fanning (b010), Mohammed's eyes are wide open instead of closed (b013), the fqih never puts a finger to his lips while boys wash in mid-air feet away from the fountain (b014), and the fqih is tiny, occluded, and standing upright during ruku prayer (b015).
